nary_nodes.label: Spider-Man dominates box office
evidence: 'Spider-Man' continues to dominate box office, passing $2 billion globally

The Sony Pictures release added another $70 million from theaters in the U.S. and Canada, bringing its domestic total to a staggering $785.8 million, making it the fourth-biggest domestic release ever.
With $118.7 million from overseas markets, it surpassed $2 billion globally, only the eighth movie ever to achieve that landmark (not accounting for inflation) and the second-fastest to do so.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event describing the financial performance of a film at the box office.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org event class fits; minting a new subtype of Event.

nary_nodes.label: The Odyssey stays second
evidence: 'The Odyssey,' now in its fifth weekend, also managed to stay in second with a $23.2 million weekend that pushed its domestic total to $504.7 million.
With $98 million from international showings, propelled by $36.6 million from its first few days playing in China, Christopher Nolan's epic has now made over $1.2 billion globally.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event describing the financial performance of a film at the box office.

nary_nodes.label: The End of Oak Street opens
evidence: 'The End of Oak Street' came in ahead of expectations with around $21 million from 3,446 locations.
It also made $26 million from international screenings, adding up to a $47 million global opening against a reported $80 million production budget.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event describing the opening of a film at the box office.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org event class fits; minting a new subtype of Event.

nary_nodes.label: Paw Patrol opens third
evidence: 'Paw Patrol: The Dino Movie' and 'The End of Oak Street,' one targeted to very young children and the other an original PG-13 rated action movie, battled for third place in their first weekend in theaters.
Family audiences showed up for 'Paw Patrol: The Dino Movie,' which Paramount Pictures released in 3,545 theaters in the U.S. and Canada this weekend.

nary_nodes.label: Katseye documentary opens
evidence: The Katseye documentary 'Katseye: Wild Hearts' rounded out the top five with $4 million from only 724 screens.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event describing the opening of a film at the box office.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org event class fits; minting a new subtype of Event.

nary_nodes.label: Other newcomers open
evidence: Several other newcomers also managed to get places in the top 10: 'Six: The Musical Live' opened in sixth place with $3 million, followed by 'The Brink of War' with $2.7 million.
The Tamil-language romance 'Vishwanath & Sons' made $1.6 million to take 10th place.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event describing the opening of a film at the box office.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org event class fits; minting a new subtype of Event.

nary_nodes.label: Rivals and Tony open
evidence: The Matthew McConaughey crime thriller 'The Rivals of Amziah King' opened outside of the top 10 with just over $1 million from 632 theaters.
The young Anthony Bourdain biopic 'Tony,' meanwhile, made $706,676 from 37 theaters in its second weekend.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event describing the opening of a film at the box office.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org event class fits; minting a new subtype of Event.

nary_nodes.label: Summer box office strong
evidence: The box office is strong with the summer season, now over, accounting for over $4.2 billion in ticket sales — about 5.7% ahead of the pre-pandemic summer of 2019.
Paul Dergarabedian, the head of marketplace trends for Rentrak, noted that the number is only about $130 million shy of the record 2013 summer, which was led by 'Iron Man 3' and 'Despicable Me 2'.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event describing the box office performance over a season.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org event class fits; minting a new subtype of Event.

nary_nodes.label: Top five summer prediction
evidence: While this summer might not surpass 2013, Dergarabedian said, 'This is going to be a top five summer of all time.'

nary_nodes.label: Audience recommendation
evidence: According to PostTrak exit polls, just over half the opening weekend audience said they would 'definitely recommend' to friends.
